business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Manufactures hygiene products across three core segments - female healthcare, adult care and baby care - from a single automated facility at Rajkot, Gujarat spread across 32,780.88 sq ft with an installed capacity of 6.41 lakh sanitary napkins/pieces per day. Core product is sanitary napkins, with Femiss addressing the economic segment, Womanica the premium high-absorbency segment, ElderFit adult hygiene and Bloom Baby baby care; sanitary napkins are also made on white label for a few customers. Products reach B2B and B2C customers pan-India through General Trade distributors (via consignment sale agents) and e-commerce platforms including Meesho, Amazon, Glowroad, Flipkart, Snapdeal and JioMart; 25 SKUs as on May 31, 2026.

group_structure.body:

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward: major raw materials are fluff pulp and superabsorbent polymers (plus top sheet, back sheet, tissue paper, air-laid paper, wing release paper and glue), sourced from suppliers in the U.S. and India. Imported raw material purchases fell from Rs 2,370.42 lakhs (46.62% of purchases) in Fiscal 2024 to Rs 1,541.23 lakhs (38.60%) in Fiscal 2025 and Rs 318.54 lakhs (5.74%) in Fiscal 2026, with domestic sourcing rising to 94.26%; total raw material purchases were Rs 5,553.17 lakhs in Fiscal 2026. The Company sourced from 88, 78 and 62 suppliers in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, does not enter into agreements with suppliers, and states that 4 of its top 10 suppliers have been associated with it for about 3 years; materials consumed were 46.24%, 42.11% and 46.30% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Manufacturing is in-house at the owned, fully automated Rajkot unit (raw material handling through to finished-product packaging), though 48.58% of Fiscal 2026 revenue came from the Trading segment rather than own manufacturing. Forward: own-brand portfolio (Femiss, Womanica, ElderFit, Bloom Baby) plus white-label manufacture, distributed pan-India through a dual-channel model - 25 Consignment Sale Agents servicing approximately 202 distributors with a sales and marketing team of over 99 personnel (offline 92.79% of Fiscal 2026 revenue), and direct e-commerce presence on Meesho, Amazon, Flipkart, Glowroad, Snapdeal, JioMart and Myntra (online 7.21%, of which Meesho alone was 6.83%). Customer base of more than 227 customers across 28 states and 8 union territories. The DRHP notes that for Customer 1 (48.35% of Fiscal 2026 revenue and 34.16% of Fiscal 2025 revenue) the Company acts as a third-party contractor executing work for a government order.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Raw material and supply chain vulnerability - the RHP identifies supply chain disruption as a combined factor affecting results of operations
- Revenue mix shift from white-label manufacturing to own brands - own brand rose from 5.37% of revenue in Fiscal 2024 to 79.06% in Fiscal 2025 and 94.47% in Fiscal 2026, while white labelling fell from 61.08% to 3.00%
- Channel mix between offline distributors (92.79% of FY2026 revenue) and e-commerce (7.21%), with Meesho the dominant online platform
- Customer concentration - top ten customers accounted for 80.41%, 78.32% and 79.57% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, with Customer 1 alone at 48.35% in Fiscal 2026
- Geographic concentration in Western India (84.42% of FY2026 revenue), with Gujarat the dominant market
- Operating leverage from a largely automated single facility - EBITDA margin improved from 8.98% (FY2024) to 12.88% (FY2025) and 13.07% (FY2026)
- Deleveraging - debt to equity fell from 4.19x (FY2024) to 0.67x (FY2025) and 0.51x (FY2026), while RoE fell from 126.65% to 30.90% on a larger equity base
- Working capital cycle - net capital turnover ratio declined from 8.81x (FY2024) to 5.22x (FY2025) and 3.18x (FY2026); current ratio 1.41x in FY2026

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Set up a new manufacturing facility at Rajkot, Gujarat ("Proposed facility Unit 2") funded from the Net Proceeds of the Fresh Offer
- Add more product and service adjacencies on the platform by leveraging brand strength, which the Company expects would further increase its customer base
- Continue to leverage the advantages of the online forum / e-commerce channel in the business
- Build brand awareness through an integrated online and offline approach - social media marketing, content marketing, SEO, targeted advertisements and rural hygiene-education campaigns
- Drive long-term retention with stockists and distributors through loyalty programs, personalised offers and timely purchase reminders for cyclical-use products
- Deepen the multi-layered customer acquisition approach using social proof, certifications and interactive digital content across e-commerce platforms and physical stores
- Prepay / repay loans and reduce leverage using Net Proceeds

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company began production in 2017-18 with an initial capacity of approximately 4 lakh units per day, launched Femiss and Womanica in 2018-19, extended distribution to North and East India in 2019-20, commenced online sales in 2022-23 and in 2023-24 added a new manufacturing line (stated in the RHP as a capacity of approximately 8 Crore pieces per day), taking installed capacity at the single Rajkot facility to 6.41 lakh sanitary napkins/pieces per day across 32,780.88 sq ft. Production volumes grew from 11.40 crore pieces per annum in Fiscal 2024 to 18.15 crore pieces per annum in Fiscal 2025, and property, plant and equipment additions of Rs 44.89, Rs 34.68 lakhs and Rs 565.23 lakhs in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 cumulatively constitute about 51.12% of gross block as of March 31, 2026. The next expansion step is a second manufacturing facility at Rajkot, Gujarat ("Proposed facility Unit 2"), to be funded with Rs 3,136.12 lakhs of Net Proceeds from the Fresh Offer; the product range was also broadened into adult diapers (ElderFit, December 2024) and baby diapers (Bloom Baby, April 2025).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Modern manufacturing facility - 32,780.88 sq ft, fully automated from raw material handling to finished product packaging with minimal human intervention, real-time monitoring and technologies sourced from China
- Dual-channel distribution of personal health and hygiene products - General Trade networks plus major e-commerce platforms, covering B2B and B2C
- Brand affinity, loyalty and trust - Femiss won the National Award for Excellence in Healthcare 2020 for 'Best Emerging Brand of the Year', Business Leadership Award 2021 for 'Innovative Product - Feminine Hygiene Ultrafluff Sanitary Pad', and 'Best Hypoallergenic Hygiene and Sanitary Brand of the Year 2025'
- Wide geographic presence in India - more than 227 customers across 28 states and 8 union territories over the last three Fiscals
- Quality and compliance credentials - ISO 9001:2015, WHO-GMP and BIS certifications with a 5-member quality team as on May 31, 2026
- Long-standing customer relationships - five customers associated with the Company for more than 5 years
- Multi-brand portfolio spanning the hygiene care spectrum from babies (Bloom Baby) to young women (Femiss, Womanica) to the elderly (ElderFit)

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Severe customer concentration — Top ten customers were 80.41% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2026 (78.32% in Fiscal 2025, 79.57% in Fiscal 2024); Customer 1 alone contributed 6,320.81 lakhs or 48.35% in Fiscal 2026, up from 34.16% in Fiscal 2025
- Dependence on a government order executed as a third-party contractor — For Customer 1 - the single largest customer at 48.35% of Fiscal 2026 revenue - the Company is a third party contractor executing work for a government order in Fiscals 2026 and 2025, making the largest revenue block non-recurring in nature
- Geographic concentration in Western India — Western India was 84.42% of Fiscal 2026 revenue from operations with Gujarat the dominant market; Northern India revenue fell from 2,749.62 lakhs (32.60%) in Fiscal 2024 to 565.08 lakhs (4.32%) in Fiscal 2026
- Single manufacturing facility — All manufacturing is concentrated at one Rajkot, Gujarat facility of 32,780.88 sq ft; any disruption there would halt production across all brands
- Dependence on imported plant technology — The facility incorporates technologies majorly sourced from China, creating exposure to import, spares, servicing and trade-policy disruption
- Outstanding legal proceedings across the Company, Group Company, Promoters, Directors and KMP/SMP — Proceedings pending at different levels of adjudication could divert management time and financial resources, and an adverse judgment could adversely affect business, financial condition and results of operations
- Change in statutory auditor shortly before the offer — The erstwhile statutory auditor resigned due to pre-occupation in other assignments w.e.f. April 21, 2026 and Savjani & Associates was appointed against the casual vacancy; future auditor changes or transition disruption may affect timely statutory audits, financial reporting and regulatory filings
- Industry data is from a commissioned, non-independently-verified report — Industry and market information is derived from the Credence Research Report, which was commissioned and paid for by the Company for an agreed fee and has not been independently verified

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Set up a new manufacturing facility at Rajkot, Gujarat ("Proposed facility Unit 2") using Rs 3,136.12 lakhs of Net Proceeds from the Fresh Offer**
- **Prepay / repay loans using Rs 356.59 lakhs of the Net Proceeds**
- **Cap the amount utilised for general corporate purposes at not more than 15% of Gross Proceeds or Rs 10 Crore, whichever is lower**
- **Continue to add more product and service adjacencies on the platform by leveraging brand strength, which the Company expects would further increase its customer base**
- **Continue to leverage the advantages of the online forum / e-commerce channel in the business**
- **Diversify beyond sanitary napkins across the hygiene care spectrum with ElderFit adult diapers (introduced December 2024) and Bloom Baby baby diapers (introduced April 2025)**
- **Operate the Rajkot facility at an installed capacity of 6.41 lakh sanitary napkins/pieces per day across 32,780.88 sq ft**
- **Grow annual production volumes, which rose from 11.40 crore pieces per annum in Fiscal 2024 to 18.15 crore pieces per annum in Fiscal 2025**
- **Maintain and extend the pan-India distribution network of 25 consignment sale agents servicing approximately 202 distributors, supported by a sales and marketing team of over 99 personnel**
- **Drive long-term retention with stockists and distributors through loyalty programs, personalised offers and timely purchase reminders for cyclical-use products, alongside rural hygiene-education campaigns**
- **Largest customer, a government order executed as a third-party contractor, accounted for 48.35% of Fiscal 2026 revenue from operations, with the top ten customers at 80.41%**
